# --instructions--

Store in the constant `makeCounter` an arrow function with the parameters `start` (default `0`) and `step` (default `1`) that returns an arrow function; every call to the returned function adds `step` to the current value and returns it, starting from `start`

# --asserts--

A counter created with `makeCounter()` must return `1`, `2` and `3` on three consecutive calls.

```javascript
tryCatch((() => { const c = makeCounter(); return c() === 1 && c() === 2 && c() === 3; })());
```

A counter created with `makeCounter(10)` must return `11` and then `12`.

```javascript
tryCatch((() => { const c = makeCounter(10); return c() === 11 && c() === 12; })());
```

A counter created with `makeCounter(0, 5)` must return `5`, `10` and `15`.

```javascript
tryCatch((() => { const c = makeCounter(0, 5); return c() === 5 && c() === 10 && c() === 15; })());
```

Two counters must be independent.

```javascript
tryCatch((() => { const a = makeCounter(); const b = makeCounter(100); a(); a(); return a() === 3 && b() === 101; })());
```

`makeCounter` must be an arrow function that returns an arrow function.

```javascript
tryCatch(!/function/.test(makeCounter.toString()) && /=>/.test(makeCounter().toString()));
```

# --solutions--

```javascript
const makeCounter = (start = 0, step = 1) => {
  let current = start;
  return () => {
    current += step;
    return current;
  };
};
```
